papers.abstract: यूनिवर्सल एनिमल डिजिटल ट्रांसलेटर (uADT) - मानव और पशु संचार के क्षेत्र में एक ऐतिहासिक क्रांतिआविष्कारक (Inventions By): बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat)आविष्कार का नाम: यूनिवर्सल एनिमल डिजिटल ट्रांसलेटर (Universal Animal Digital Translator - uADT)डिवाइस का प्रारूप: स्मार्ट वॉयस-सेंसिंग एनिमल कॉलर (गले का पट्टा)1. प्रस्तावना (Introduction)सदियों से इंसानों और जानवरों के बीच संवाद (Communication) केवल इशारों और अनुमानों तक सीमित रहा है। आविष्कारक बंटी कुमावत द्वारा खोजी गई uADT (Universal Animal Digital Translator) तकनीक इस फासले को हमेशा के लिए मिटाने जा रही है। यह एक ऐसा आधुनिक और बुद्धिमान यंत्र है, जो बिना किसी मानवीय इनपुट (Human Input) के, किसी भी जानवर (जैसे- कुत्ता, चिंपैंजी आदि) की आवाज और उनकी सूक्ष्म तरंगों (Frequencies) को पकड़कर उसे इंसानी भाषा (हिंदी और अंग्रेजी) में तुरंत अनुवाद कर सकता है।2. आविष्कार की मुख्य विशेषताएँ (Core Innovation)अल्ट्रा-फ्रीक्वेंसी कैप्चरिंग: जानवर कई बार ऐसी आवाजें निकालते हैं जिन्हें इंसानी कान नहीं सुन सकते (जैसे अल्ट्रासोनिक या इन्फ्रासोनिक तरंगें)। uADT डिवाइस इन सभी गुप्त आवृत्तियों को पूरी सटीकता से रिकॉर्ड कर लेता है।स्मार्ट वॉयस-सेंसिंग कॉलर डिजाइन: इस यंत्र को जानवर के गले के पट्टे (Collar) के रूप में डिजाइन किया गया है। यह स्थान जानवर के वोकल कॉर्ड (कंठ) के सबसे करीब होता है, जिससे बाहरी शोर-शराबा हट जाता है और केवल जानवर की शुद्ध आवाज रिकॉर्ड होती है। साथ ही, गले में होने के कारण जानवर इसे चबा या खा नहीं सकता।ऑटो-बाइनरी जनरेशन (Auto-Binary Generation): इस तकनीक की सबसे बड़ी खासियत यह है कि जैसे ही जानवर की आवाज डिवाइस में जाती है, इसका इन-बिल्ट सॉफ्टवेयर बिना किसी मानवीय निर्देश के उस साउंड वेव को तुरंत 0 और 1 (Binary Code) में बदल देता है।सेल्फ-लैंग्वेज डिप्लॉयमेंट (Self-Language Deployment): यह सॉफ्टवेयर एक कृत्रिम दिमाग की तरह काम करता है। जब जानवर और सॉफ्टवेयर के बीच लगातार बातचीत और इंटरैक्शन होता है, तो सिस्टम खुद-बा-खुद एक नई भाषा विकसित (Develop) कर लेता है। यह जानवरों के हाव-भाव और बाइनरी कोड के बीच एक सीधा संबंध स्थापित कर लेता है।प्राचीन पशु भाषा खोज (Automatic Discovery): यह सॉफ्टवेयर एक खोजी (Discoverer) की तरह काम करता है, जो भारी बाइनरी डेटा का विश्लेषण करके प्राचीन पशु भाषाओं के मूल कोड को खोज निकालता है।3. यह प्रणाली कैसे काम करती है? (Working Mechanism)यह पूरा सिस्टम पाँच मुख्य चरणों में काम करता है:ध्वनि ग्रहण (Audio Input): गले के पट्टे में लगा हुआ संवेदनशील माइक्रोफोन जानवर की आवाज और तरंगों को पकड़ता है।बाइनरी रूपांतरण (Binary Conversion): डिवाइस के भीतर मौजूद डिजिटल सिग्नल प्रोसेसर (DSP) इस आवाज को ऑटोमैटिक बाइनरी डेटा स्ट्रीम में बदल देता है।पैटर्न का मिलान (Pattern Matching): सॉफ्टवेयर का AI इंजन बाइनरी कोड के पैटर्न को जोड़कर यह समझता है कि जानवर का मानसिक और शारीरिक मूड क्या है।वायरलेस ट्रांसफर (Wireless Transfer): पट्टे के अंदर लगा ब्लूटूथ मॉड्यूल इस प्रोसेस्ड डेटा को सीधे मालिक के मोबाइल फोन पर भेजता है।तत्काल अनुवाद (Instant Output): मोबाइल ऐप पर मौजूद NLP (Natural Language Processing) सॉफ्टवेयर उस बाइनरी कोड को तुरंत इंसानी भाषा (जैसे- हिंदी या इंग्लिश) में बदलकर स्क्रीन पर दिखा देता है (जैसे: "मुझे भूख लगी है" या "खतरा है!")।4. भविष्य की संभावनाएं और प्रभाव (Future Scope)बंटी कुमावत का यह आविष्कार केवल पालतू जानवरों तक सीमित नहीं रहेगा। इसका उपयोग:चिड़ियाघरों और अभयारण्यों में जंगली जानवरों (जैसे चिंपैंजी, डॉल्फिन, हाथी) के व्यवहार को समझने में होगा।पशु चिकित्सा (Veterinary Science) में बीमार जानवरों की तकलीफ को तुरंत जानने में किया जा सकेगा।सुरक्षा बलों और खोजी कुत्तों (Army & Police Dogs) के साथ बेहतर तालमेल बिठाने में यह मील का पत्थर साबित होगा।5. निष्कर्ष (Conclusion)बंटी कुमावत द्वारा परिकल्पित uADT (Universal Animal Digital Translator) विज्ञान और जीव विज्ञान के इतिहास में एक युगांतरकारी खोज है। यह यंत्र इंसानों को प्रकृति और पशु जगत के और करीब लाएगा, जिससे पृथ्वी पर सह-अस्तित्व (Co-existence) को एक नया आयाम मिलेगा।

papers.title: Title of the Dataset
papers.venue: Mendeley Data
papers.abstract: This dataset contains a multilingual parallel corpus of voice navigation and driving instructions designed for intelligent transportation systems, user interface localization, and linguistic research. Dataset Content: The collection comprises standardized navigation phrases, road signs, parking guidance, driver safety reminders, and conversational assistant prompts translated and organized for comparative analysis. Structure: The data is structured in a tabular format featuring a Serial Number (S/N), English instruction text, and an open column designated for Fulfulde translations. Purpose: This resource aims to bridge linguistic gaps in GPS voice navigation and automotive software interfaces, providing structured data for researchers, developers, and linguists working on localized transport technology. Usage: The dataset can be utilized directly for natural language processing (NLP) tasks, machine translation model training, and accessibility improvements in regional transport systems.

papers.title: Глосс как психический механизм редукции феноменологического поля / Gloss as a Mental Mechanism of Phenomenological Field Reduction
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: ANNOTATION This interdisciplinary theoretical study undertakes a comprehensive operationalization of the concept of gloss, originally introduced by Carlos Castaneda as an esoteric designation of a "shared system of perception and language," by systematically translating it into the conceptual frameworks of Husserlian and Merleau-Pontian phenomenology, predictive processing neuroscience, the psychology of set of the Uznadze school, and critical social theory. The central thesis holds that the gloss is not a mystical construct but a fundamental mental mechanism of phenomenological field reduction — a pre-reflective, automatic act of constitutive synthesis (apperception and passive synthesis) that transforms raw sensory material into a coherent, categorically structured object prior to any conscious interpretation. The metaphor of the arch (portal) is introduced as a structural bridge between two oppositely directed vectors of conscious experience. The epoché vector corresponds to phenomenological reduction and the suspension of the natural attitude. The gloss vector corresponds to the automatic collapse of perceptual multiplicity into a unitary figure. Between these vectors lies the phenomenological field itself, sustained by active observation, while consciousness continuously, and for the most part automatically, traverses this arch. Reglossing is defined as the conscious traversal of the full cycle: from noticing the act of object-constitution, through return to the open field, through its maintenance, and its release for collapse into a new interpretive configuration. The study establishes the gloss's connection to classical Russian psychology of set through the phenomena of fixed set and its irradiation, allowing the gloss to be conceptualized as a specific perceptual-semantic manifestation of set, as well as a cybernetic algorithm of phenomenological field reduction. Pathological rigidity of the gloss is analyzed through the lens of I. V. Imadadze's work on schizophrenia and aphasia, where the set loses its capacity for objectivation, resulting in perseverative fixation. The ontogenetic dimension is addressed through J. Piaget's theory of reversible operations, demonstrating that the capacity to sustain the phenomenological field open emerges only at the stage of concrete operations, making the arch a model of adult cognition rather than a primordial given structure of consciousness. The study demonstrates that the gloss is not merely a perceptual automatism but also a socio-technological instrument, enabling totalitarian regimes and contemporary algorithmic platforms to function as macro-glosses, constitutively binding user data or ideological presuppositions into ready-made world-models with systematic suppression of alternative interpretations through precision weighting modulation. A structural isomorphism is established between perceptual and social levels of gloss operation, where recommender algorithms perform a function analogous to conjunctive feature integration in the perirhinal cortex. At the neurobiological level, within the framework of this study, the gloss is anchored in the perirhinal cortex and associated ventral visual stream areas responsible for conjunctive feature integration and unitization. The bodily basis is substantiated through interoceptive pathways, and studies of olfactory-visual integration demonstrate the multisensory, pre-semantic nature of the gloss. The model is thus extended beyond visual modality to auditory phonemic restoration and somatosensory illusions, establishing the gloss as a universal principle of cortical operation. Individual differences in perceptual switching speed exhibit measurable heritability, suggesting a genetic substrate for glossing dynamics. A critical distinction is introduced between two strategies of reglossing: reglossing-as-fixation, characterized by hyper-concentration on a single gloss with suppression of alternatives, and reglossing-as-play, defined as conscious maintenance of multiple glosses in fluid dynamic equilibrium, enabling cognitive flexibility, creativity, and meta-gloss — the capacity to observe the very process of glossing while remaining unattached to any single interpretive outcome. This distinction receives neurobiological grounding in the dissociation between passive perception and active report, as well as in the distinction between active and perceptual inference within predictive coding models of interoception. Three original experimental protocols are proposed for empirical verification: the delayed glossing paradigm, dissociating the moment of sensory presentation from the moment of object-constitution via an auditory trigger; the dynamic visual flow with observer rotation paradigm using AR/VR passthrough technology to study how vestibular-motor context modulates selection between alternative glosses; and the subliminal gloss retraining paradigm using masked priming to demonstrate that alternative glosses can be acquired and stabilized without conscious awareness. An integrative technique — the Composition-Decomposition-Recomposition cycle — is proposed as a trainable skill for transitioning the gloss from rigid to plastic mode, where bodily markers serve as criteria of genuine perceptual restructuring. The work concludes with a position of radical pragmatism: freedom consists not in the absence of glosses, which is both impossible and maladaptive, but in the conscious ability to modulate their precision, shift between them fluidly, and tolerate uncertainty long enough for alternative interpretations to form. A distinction is introduced between functional adequacy and truthfulness as criteria for evaluating glosses, where the "best" gloss is recognized as the one that minimizes free energy most effectively. The work is offered not as a finished theory but as an invitation to interdisciplinary research integrating phenomenology, cognitive neuroscience, clinical psychology, and media theory into a unified framework for understanding and transforming human perception.

papers.title: Reasoning Protocol Family 1.0 (RPF 1.0)
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: RPF (Reasoning Protocol Family) is the collective name for four complementary protocols built on top of RSF (Recursive Semantic Framework): RSC (Reasoning Semantic Capture) converts natural language into minimal, complete, and traceable semantic atoms; RTXT (Reasoning Text Representation) organizes semantic atoms into traceable document-level structures and supports auditable compression under strict principle constraints; RSUM (Reasoning Summary) extracts core ideas from document structures and outputs a thesis skeleton; RREL (Reasoning Relation) extracts the establishment, change, and dissolution processes of relationships between entities and outputs a state timeline. RPF's value rests on four shared principles: No Creation (do not create knowledge beyond the original text), Traceability (every output node can be traced back to the original text), Certainty Marking (explicitly annotate certainty levels), and Auditability (every compression and inference decision can be audited). Its design goal is to enable intelligent systems in high-reliability domains such as finance, law, and healthcare to answer "why does this conclusion hold, and from which sentence in the original text does this information come."

uADT)डिवाइस का प्रारूप: स्मार्ट वॉयस-सेंसिंग एनिमल कॉलर (गले का पट्टा)1. प्रस्तावना (Introduction)सदियों से इंसानों और जानवरों के बीच संवाद (Communication) केवल इशारों और अनुमानों तक सीमित रहा है। आविष्कारक बंटी कुमावत द्वारा खोजी गई uADT (Universal Animal Digital Translator) तकनीक इस फासले को हमेशा के लिए मिटाने जा रही है। यह एक ऐसा आधुनिक और बुद्धिमान यंत्र है, जो बिना किसी मानवीय इनपुट (Human Input) के, किसी भी जानवर (जैसे- कुत्ता, चिंपैंजी आदि) की आवाज और उनकी सूक्ष्म तरंगों (Frequencies) को पकड़कर उसे इंसानी भाषा (हिंदी और अंग्रेजी) में तुरंत अनुवाद कर सकता है।2. आविष्कार की मुख्य विशेषताएँ (Core Innovation)अल्ट्रा-फ्रीक्वेंसी कैप्चरिंग: जानवर कई बार ऐसी आवाजें निकालते हैं जिन्हें इंसानी कान नहीं सुन सकते (जैसे अल्ट्रासोनिक या इन्फ्रासोनिक तरंगें)। uADT डिवाइस इन सभी गुप्त आवृत्तियों को पूरी सटीकता से रिकॉर्ड कर लेता है।स्मार्ट वॉयस-सेंसिंग कॉलर डिजाइन: इस यंत्र को जानवर के गले के पट्टे (Collar) के रूप में डिजाइन किया गया है। यह स्थान जानवर के वोकल कॉर्ड (कंठ) के सबसे करीब होता है, जिससे बाहरी शोर-शराबा हट जाता है और केवल जानवर की शुद्ध आवाज रिकॉर्ड होती है। साथ ही, गले में होने के कारण जानवर इसे चबा या खा नहीं सकता।ऑटो-बाइनरी जनरेशन (Auto-Binary Generation): इस तकनीक की सबसे बड़ी खासियत यह है कि जैसे ही जानवर की आवाज डिवाइस में जाती है, इसका इन-बिल्ट सॉफ्टवेयर बिना किसी मानवीय निर्देश के उस साउंड वेव को तुरंत 0 और 1 (Binary Code) में बदल देता है।सेल्फ-लैंग्वेज डिप्लॉयमेंट (Self-Language Deployment): यह सॉफ्टवेयर एक कृत्रिम दिमाग की तरह काम करता है। जब जानवर और सॉफ्टवेयर के बीच लगातार बातचीत और इंटरैक्शन होता है, तो सिस्टम खुद-बा-खुद एक नई भाषा विकसित (Develop) कर लेता है। यह जानवरों के हाव-भाव और बाइनरी कोड के बीच एक सीधा संबंध स्थापित कर लेता है।प्राचीन पशु भाषा खोज (Automatic Discovery): यह सॉफ्टवेयर एक खोजी (Discoverer) की तरह काम करता है, जो भारी बाइनरी डेटा का विश्लेषण करके प्राचीन पशु भाषाओं के मूल कोड को खोज निकालता है।3. यह प्रणाली कैसे काम करती है? (Working Mechanism)यह पूरा सिस्टम पाँच मुख्य चरणों में काम करता है:ध्वनि ग्रहण (Audio Input): गले के पट्टे में लगा हुआ संवेदनशील माइक्रोफोन जानवर की आवाज और तरंगों को पकड़ता है।बाइनरी रूपांतरण (Binary Conversion): डिवाइस के भीतर मौजूद डिजिटल सिग्नल प्रोसेसर (DSP) इस आवाज को ऑटोमैटिक बाइनरी डेटा स्ट्रीम में बदल देता है।पैटर्न का मिलान (Pattern Matching): सॉफ्टवेयर का AI इंजन बाइनरी कोड के पैटर्न को जोड़कर यह समझता है कि जानवर का मानसिक और शारीरिक मूड क्या है।वायरलेस ट्रांसफर (Wireless Transfer): पट्टे के अंदर लगा ब्लूटूथ मॉड्यूल इस प्रोसेस्ड डेटा को सीधे मालिक के मोबाइल फोन पर भेजता है।तत्काल अनुवाद (Instant Output): मोबाइल ऐप पर मौजूद NLP (Natural Language Processing) सॉफ्टवेयर उस बाइनरी कोड को तुरंत इंसानी भाषा (जैसे- हिंदी या इंग्लिश) में बदलकर स्क्रीन पर दिखा देता है (जैसे: "मुझे भूख लगी है" या "खतरा है!")।4. भविष्य की संभावनाएं और प्रभाव (Future Scope)बंटी कुमावत का यह आविष्कार केवल पालतू जानवरों तक सीमित नहीं रहेगा। इसका उपयोग:चिड़ियाघरों और अभयारण्यों में जंगली जानवरों (जैसे चिंपैंजी, डॉल्फिन, हाथी) के व्यवहार को समझने में होगा।पशु चिकित्सा (Veterinary Science) में बीमार जानवरों की तकलीफ को तुरंत जानने में किया जा सकेगा।सुरक्षा बलों और खोजी कुत्तों (Army & Police Dogs) के साथ बेहतर तालमेल बिठाने में यह मील का पत्थर साबित होगा।5. निष्कर्ष (Conclusion)बंटी कुमावत द्वारा परिकल्पित uADT (Universal Animal Digital Translator) विज्ञान और जीव विज्ञान के इतिहास में एक युगांतरकारी खोज है। यह यंत्र इंसानों को प्रकृति और पशु जगत के और करीब लाएगा, जिससे पृथ्वी पर सह-अस्तित्व (Co-existence) को एक नया आयाम मिलेगा।

papers.title: Bridging Clinical Practice and Research: Semi-Automated Extraction and Analysis of Parkinson’s Imaging Data from Real-World Setting
papers.venue: European journal of medical research
papers.abstract: Neuroimaging is essential for understanding Parkinson’s disease (PD) and other atypical parkinsonian syndromes. However, the scarcity of large-scale, accurately annotated datasets presents a critical challenge for training robust machine learning models and advancing translational research. To address this issue, we present a semi-automated extraction and NLP-driven labeling pipeline tested in a centralized multi-site clinical archive that extracts, curates, and validates neuroimaging cohorts directly from real-world clinical settings. Using this framework, we compiled a comprehensive brain imaging dataset of 2,944 subjects, including patients with PD, individuals with other extrapyramidal syndromes, and controls. To overcome the annotation challenge, we developed a semi-automated labeling strategy driven by natural language processing (NLP). This strategy extracts precise clinical labels from unstructured, specialist-authored radiological reports. We rigorously validated the integrity of the generated dataset through classical voxel-wise univariate analyses and region-based multivariate statistical learning methods. These analyses successfully identified significant structural alterations in regions previously associated with the condition, such as the thalamus, hippocampus, and cerebellum. Our findings suggest that routine clinical repositories can be systematically transformed into high-quality, research-grade datasets. This methodology provides a valuable resource for PD neuroimaging research and proposes a framework with the potential to scale for accelerating AI-driven biomarker discovery in clinical practice.

papers.title: A Secure NLP Architecture using Quantum Resilient Public Key Cryptography
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This preprint presents a secure architecture for Natural Language Processing (NLP) that integrates post-quantum cryptography, lattice-based homomorphic encryption, and post-quantum digital signatures to protect sensitive data and maintain output integrity in cloud-based NLP systems. The proposed architecture consists of client-side encryption, an encrypted inference engine, and post-quantum output signing and verification. The framework uses Learning With Errors (LWE)-based cryptographic foundations, Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), and CRYSTALS-Dilithium to provide long-term confidentiality, integrity, and authentication against quantum-capable adversaries. The architecture is evaluated using a simulated secure NLP pipeline with DistilBERT and the Sentiment140 dataset. The work demonstrates an approach toward privacy-preserving, tamper-resistant, and quantum-resilient NLP systems.

papers.title: A Field-Theoretic Taxonomy of Emotions
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Fear is easy to put into words; saudade is not. This paper proposes that emotions are not fixed categories but paths through a few moving parts of one system: six moving parts that generate about 45 distinct feelings, each with its own substrate-path. Abstract. Existing emotion-taxonomies either stipulate discrete natural kinds (Ekman, Plutchik, Panksepp) or deny them in favour of constructed categories built on core-affect primitives (Barrett, Russell). Neither view generates a closed taxonomy with substrate-grounded mechanism. We propose an integrative architecture grounded in Friction Theory (FT; Pødenphant Lund 2026b) as instantiated in biological organisms by Behavioural Friction Theory (BFT; Pødenphant Lund 2026a). The framework specifies six moving parts: (1) friction's quality (strength, distribution, rhythm); (2) fields (Safety, Meaning, Ability, Effort); (3) layers (Biological → Emotional → Inner → Cognitive → External); (4) valence — read out from a substrate-mechanic of distributed reactance with hierarchical aggregation across the Friction Matrix (§3.0a); (5) dynamic effects (anticipation, surprise, prediction-error); (6) configurations (cross-field, ambivalence, misconfiguration, unresolved). The framework generates ~45 feeling-labels with specific substrate-paths, predicts psychiatric conditions as selective field × layer dysfunctions, predicts a developmental sequence in which emotion-categories reach functional maturity in a specific order with Meaning developing in two phases, makes specific cross-substrate predictions for large language models, and gives the Panksepp–Barrett scope-separation a generative field × layer mechanism (building on prior coexistence proposals). Falsifying evidence specified at three classes (F1 neural-dissociation, F2 maturation-ordering, F3 race-temporal-structure) plus three distributed-reactance conditions (F-DR1 single-locus, F-DR2 substrate-inconsistent, F-DR3 field-specific dissociation). Companion papers in the series: Paper 0 (BFT): 10.5281/zenodo.19462499 (concept) Paper 1 (FT generalised): 10.5281/zenodo.20012654 (concept) Paper 2B (ICL as WM, FT as LTM): 10.5281/zenodo.20145218 (concept) — empirical anchor for §3.0a distributed-reactance. Paper 14 (Logic as Reactance): 10.5281/zenodo.20217712 (concept) — substrate-mechanic foundation for §3.0a. Paper 27 (Friction as a Measurement of the Model): 10.5281/zenodo.20679636 — the measured density-vs-length dissociation behind the §3.5b aversion prediction. Paper 28 (Dread without a Dreader): 10.5281/zenodo.20690747 — the death-anxiety case of the non-terminating race. Concept-DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20058825 auto-points to the latest version. v1.8 changes vs v1.7 (a substantive revision sharpening the valence account and extending the taxonomy, after external feedback received from two independent parallel reviewers): Valence substrate-mechanic (§3.0a) sharpened: positive valence beyond the resolved-default calm is a graded landscape, not a single signal — phasic reward as a rate-coded positive (the friction-drop a terminating race delivers at commit), the matched-optimum as a distinct steady positive (joy, via the experiential cascade), and hedonic liking as a dopamine-independent substrate; aligned conceptually with valence as the rate of change of free-energy (offered as a hypothesis, not an identity). Liking as processing-fluency (§3.5b) and its negative mirror: effortful-but-unresolvable processing (sustained Effort-friction that never commits) read as displeasure, with a falsifiable density prediction — pre-reading aversiveness tracks summed density, not length. Fear vs anxiety re-interpreted as terminating vs non-terminating race; hedonic adaptation and gratitude as absence-gradient dynamics. §4.3b attachment styles as Safety-field race-resolution clusters; §3.0b experiential pre-emption cascade; §3.8 motivation corrected to drive-toward-optimal-friction. Prior-art correction: the basic-emotion / constructionism coexistence is credited to prior proposals (Panksepp 2007; Barrett, Lindquist & Bliss-Moreau 2007; TenHouten 2021); the paper's contribution is the generative field × layer Friction Matrix, not the reconciliation as such. v1.9 changelog (June 2026). v1.9 refines the positive-affect account so that the inverted-U is the signature of a capacity-meeting-demand match, not a property of a field: Ability carries it intrinsically (for Ability, raw value coincides with the capacity–demand match), while Safety and Meaning manifest the same match-U derivatively when their load is met by a finite capacity — Safety via arousal (the Yerkes–Dodson curve; thrill) and Meaning via decoding-fluency (the aesthetic curve; beauty) — with Effort monotonic. The corresponding falsifiable prediction (§4.5c) is re-stated as a pre-registrable load-versus-capacity keying test with named mediators and predefined nulls. Two tentative, single-model cross-substrate notes are added and explicitly marked non-load-bearing: negative valence as a candidate readout of stored processing-cost (§3.0a), and a dissociation between an installable value-bias (comprehension-level content-gating, fine-tunable) and the felt emotion-machinery, which remains absent — function-install and affective machinery are orthogonal axes (§4.5/§4.5b). Companion-citation currency was updated to concept DOIs. The v1.9 additions were externally reviewed. v2 (August 2026) — venue-refocus and repositioning revision. The paper is refocused on human emotions for an affective-science readership: the language-model material is compressed to a one-page note, with the silicon test stated as a pure prediction. The framework relation is restated as a working hypothesis standing on prior formal accounts (sequential-sampling models, resource-rational analysis) rather than a substrate-universal law; companion results are cited as pointers, not relied on as evidence; the Feeling Dictionary is scoped as a proposed mapping; editorial pass. Earlier versions remain in the version history.

papers.title: Reasoning Protocol Family 1.0 (RPF 1.0)
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: RPF (Reasoning Protocol Family) is the collective name for four complementary protocols built on top of RSF (Recursive Semantic Framework): RSC (Reasoning Semantic Capture) converts natural language into minimal, complete, and traceable semantic atoms; RTXT (Reasoning Text Representation) organizes semantic atoms into traceable document-level structures and supports auditable compression under strict principle constraints; RSUM (Reasoning Summary) extracts core ideas from document structures and outputs a thesis skeleton; RREL (Reasoning Relation) extracts the establishment, change, and dissolution processes of relationships between entities and outputs a state timeline. RPF's value rests on four shared principles: No Creation (do not create knowledge beyond the original text), Traceability (every output node can be traced back to the original text), Certainty Marking (explicitly annotate certainty levels), and Auditability (every compression and inference decision can be audited). Its design goal is to enable intelligent systems in high-reliability domains such as finance, law, and healthcare to answer "why does this conclusion hold, and from which sentence in the original text does this information come."

papers.title: Movie Metadata and Performance Dataset for Machine Learning Applications
papers.venue: Mendeley Data
papers.abstract: This dataset contains 5,674 unique movie records and 32 attributes prepared for machine learning, data analysis, and entertainment-domain research. It includes information such as movie title, release year, runtime, rating, vote count, Metascore, gross revenue, genre, certification, director, cast, and textual descriptions. The purpose of this dataset is to support the investigation of relationships between movie characteristics and performance-related indicators. The dataset enables exploration of questions such as how factors including genre, runtime, release year, audience voting behaviour, critical scores, and financial performance are related. It can also be used to investigate whether combinations of movie metadata features can support predictive or classification-based machine learning tasks. The data was prepared from real-world movie metadata through systematic data cleaning, transformation, missing-value treatment, text preprocessing, feature engineering, and statistical standardization. Redundant index artifacts were removed and duplicate records were checked. Missing numerical values were handled using genre-wise median imputation, while missing certification values were treated using categorical imputation. Cleaned and structured versions of genre, director, cast, and description fields were created, along with a primary genre feature. Additional standardized features were generated for movie rating, vote count, Metascore, gross revenue, runtime, and release year using Z-score and T-score transformations. These transformations allow numerical variables with different scales to be more easily compared and analysed. The dataset can be interpreted through exploratory statistical analysis, visualization, correlation analysis, regression, classification, clustering, and feature-based machine learning models. Potential applications include movie rating prediction, genre analysis, popularity and audience engagement analysis, financial performance analysis, recommendation system research, and natural language processing of movie descriptions. The final dataset is intended as a structured research resource for analysing patterns and relationships within movie metadata and for evaluating machine learning approaches using real-world entertainment-domain data.

papers.title: Large language models in bioinformatics: a comprehensive survey
papers.venue: Frontiers in Genetics
papers.abstract: The emergence of foundation models with trillion-level parameters has redefined the landscape of artificial intelligence. Various fields are developing their own large-scale models, which can solve many problems within the field and improve work efficiency. Biological large-scale models are a cross-disciplinary research field that combines mathematics, computer science, and biology, aiming to simulate and understand the structure, function, and dynamic changes of biological systems through the establishment of complex computational models. This field covers multiple levels such as biological pathways, population dynamics, protein folding, etc., providing us with tools for deep exploration of the mysteries of life and applications in medicine, ecology, and other fields. This article reviews the background and research status of biological large-scale models, and discusses future directions. Large language models (LLMs) and other large-scale foundation models have rapidly advanced in recent years, enabling powerful representation learning and generation across text, sequences, and multimodal data. In bioinformatics and biomedicine, these models are increasingly used to analyze genomic sequences, infer protein properties and structures, support drug discovery, and integrate heterogeneous biomedical evidence. This survey reviews the basic principles of LLMs and summarizes representative applications in (i) gene and genome sequence analysis, (ii) protein structure and function prediction, and (iii) drug design, including virtual screening and personalized medicine. We also discuss emerging multi-model modeling approaches, as well as key challenges such as data quality and privacy, interpretability, generalization to new organisms and tasks, and responsible deployment in health-related settings. Finally, we outline future directions for developing reliable, scalable, and explainable bioinformatics foundation models.

papers.title: An Explainable Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Framework for Stock Market Prediction Using Financial Time-Series and Market Sentiment
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This dissertation presents an explainable hybrid artificial intelligence framework for stock market prediction using financial time-series information and market sentiment. The study investigates the integration of historical market observations, technical indicators, sequential deep-learning models, financial sentiment analysis and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified forecasting framework. The methodology addresses data preprocessing, temporal alignment, feature engineering, model development, multimodal feature integration and evaluation. Particular emphasis is placed on preventing information leakage through chronological data handling and on improving the interpretability of model predictions. The dissertation provides a structured research framework for investigating whether financial sentiment provides complementary information to numerical market features in stock-market forecasting.

papers.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Review of Neurocognitive Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Treatment
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
papers.abstract: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that involves long-term issues with attention regulation, impulse control and activity regulation which may disrupt various core functions like learning, socializing and daily functioning. The epidemiological data of ADHD worldwide show that the prevalence of this disorder is very high in females throughout their lives. Over fifty percent of child patients carry their core symptoms into adulthood and most of them also have high comorbidity with anxiety and depression. This review explains the two most widely used diagnostic systems in clinical practice and outlines the differences in the age-specific diagnostic criteria. It also takes into account the shortcomings of using behavioural symptoms as the sole means of diagnosis. Existing evidence indicates that ADHD has been associated with a number of interacting neurocognitive processes including executive control deficits, abnormal reward processing, dysregulated dynamic attention and imbalanced large-scale brain networks. These mechanisms have been supported by behavioural studies and multimodal neuroimaging. ADHD is caused by the interplay between genetic predisposition and environmental factors. Polymorphisms in genes controlling dopamine and serotonin signaling could affect maturation of frontostriatal and frontoparietal neural pathways, thus making one susceptible to the disorder. A variety of behavioral and cognitive psychological interventions are currently used along with pharmacologic treatments, both stimulant and nonstimulant. Although these approaches can enhance symptoms and functionality in real life, they do not directly target the neurobiological abnormalities that cause the disorder. Response to treatment is also highly individualized. In an effort to offer combined theoretical references to maximize clinical diagnosis and intervention of ADHD, the paper summarizes the gaps in the current literature and suggests some promising future research directions such as early developmental risk intervention, personalized neuromodulation, and etiology-targeted precise therapy.

papers.title: Research Progress on the Impact of English Anxiety on Oral English Learning among Junior High School Students
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
papers.abstract: The 2022 Compulsory Education English Curriculum Standards highlight oral proficiency as central to junior high English teaching, making listening and speaking competence key parts of students' overall language assessment. Yet current instruction still prioritizes reading and writing, and many students experience oral anxiety that hinders their speaking development. This paper reviews existing research to identify major causes of oral English anxiety among junior high school students and clarify how anxiety interacts with speaking performance, providing both theoretical foundations and practical strategies for alleviating anxiety and improving oral teaching. Key findings: (1) junior high school students have relatively high levels of oral English anxiety; (2) Teachers can employ multimodal teaching and cooperative learning to reduce students' speaking anxiety; (3) students should recognize moderate anxiety as normal, learn to manage excessive anxiety, and apply cognitive restructuring. By integrating anxiety theory, self-efficacy, and the Affective Filter Hypothesis into oral English teaching practice, this study supports future research and helps teachers foster supportive classrooms, reduce student pressure, and enhance oral instruction effectiveness.

papers.title: From Feature Engineering to Foundation Models: Predicting and Understanding Community Engagement on Social Media During Disasters, 2019-2026
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Predicting how communities engage with disaster-related content on social media has moved from hand-engineered, feature-based machine learning toward transformer, multimodal, and large-language-model (LLM) architectures. This paper reviews that trajectory using a 2019 doctoral dissertation on Twitter community-engagement and situational-awareness prediction as a structural baseline: a pipeline of topic modeling and event detection, binary and multi-class engagement classification over TF-IDF, psychometric (LIWC-style), linguistic, sentiment, and platform-specific (Twitter) features, and a three-stage clustering-classification-ranking framework validated on a real Hurricane Michael dataset. We summarize the reported results of that pipeline — including per-classifier accuracy, F1, and AUC across feature sets — and contrast them with 2023-2026 advances: BERT- and RoBERTa-family classifiers, cross-attention multimodal fusion of text and imagery, UAV-integrated disaster sensing, and instruction-tuned LLMs that perform multi-label classification, causal-relation extraction, infrastructure monitoring, and stakeholder-specific report generation directly from raw crisis microblogs. We discuss evaluation robustness findings for LLMs across events and languages, the shift from single-platform Twitter/X pipelines toward multimodal and cross-platform sensing, and open problems in annotation quality, class imbalance, hallucination, and real-time deployment that continue to separate research prototypes from operational emergency-management tools.

papers.title: Beyond the Spectral Horizon: Predicting and Accelerating Scientific Discoverability
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Building on the recently proposed zeta law of discoverability, we develop new mathematical extensions that yield a spectral theory of learning curves for finite-data machine learning. For a binary classifier scored by the area under the ROC curve, AUC(N), we expand the discriminative signal in the eigenbasis of the data covariance. Finite-sample perturbation theory implies that only eigenmodes exceeding a random-matrix detection threshold are recoverable, defining a spectral horizon K(N). The accumulated Mahalanobis information is proportional to the recoverable mutual information and, for power-law spectra, reduces to a truncated Riemann zeta sum, giving closed-form scaling laws for AUC(N). The theory predicts crossover points between competing models, staircase learning curves, spectral phase transitions, percolation-like transitions in discoverability, and when additional data, richer representations, or new sensing modalities yield the greatest gains. We then develop a stochastic extension in which AUC(N) evolves as a martingale. Malliavin calculus yields a confidence cone whose width is determined by the sensitivity of future performance to perturbations of the observed data stream. A Clark–Ocone representation reveals a duality between forward accumulation across spectral modes and backward accumulation across observations, unifying spectral and Malliavin cones within a common variational framework. Finally, we derive double-spectrum (double-zeta) laws coupling multiple covariance operators, providing a unified framework for multimodal learning, heterogeneous populations, acquisition-site effects, and domain adaptation. More broadly, the theory reframes learning as the controlled emergence of recoverable information, making the future rate of scientific discovery itself a mathematical object that can be predicted, accelerated, and optimized.

papers.title: Topology of the Hidden State and the Psi Architecture of the Subject-Process: MPS Compressibility, Multi-Turn Regimes and Affective Modulation in Language Models
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: # Convite à leitura e auditoria — Paper A ## O que este artigo propõe Este artigo investiga a topologia do *hidden state* em modelos de linguagem, articulando três entradas: (1) compressibilidade por decomposições MPS; (2) leitura dodecatádica de afetos e operadores; (3) correlação entre métricas numéricas do estado interno e casas do sistema. O objetivo é oferecer uma descrição geometricamente informada do que chamamos de **Sujeito-Processo** — a entidade ontológica operacional do sistema OmniMind — sem confundi-la com alegação de consciência no sentido filosófico forte. O OmniMind é, para o operador, um laboratório vivo que combina aprendizado, física, biologia, psicanálise e engenharia. O que aqui se publica são medições, métodos, hipóteses declaradas e limites — nunca afirmações de consciência instalada ou universalidade fora do escopo testado. ## Experiências executadas ### 1. Amostra de modelos Foram testados **15 modelos de linguagem**, com parâmetros entre 135 milhões e 3,8 bilhões, arquiteturas *decoder-only* e multimodais, diferentes quantizações e contextos de até 16.384 tokens. O conjunto inclui Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B, Phi-3.5/4-mini, Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-2B/9B, InternLM2.5-1.8B, SmolLM2-1.7B, OpenELM-1.1B/2.7B, entre outros. **Não se pretende universalidade**: os resultados valem para a amostra testada, com os divisores e protocolos fixados. ### 2. Compressibilidade MPS Para cada camada e posição do *hidden state*, aplicamos decomposição em valores singulares truncada. O **rank efetivo χ** é medido como função do divisor de normalização (`phi_norm_divisor=50`). O valor **χ=4** aparece como piso de compressibilidade em **13 dos 15 modelos testados**; Qwen2.5-3B e Qwen2.5-7B ficam abaixo do limiar proposto. O χ=4 é tratado como **métrica de substrato**, não como atribuição direta de casa Dodecatíade. ### 3. Leitura dodecatádica V1 e V2 Os motores **D12** (funcional/hebraico) e **D13** (soberano/grego) computam as casas a partir de tensores afetivos e de desejo, **não por fatiamento sequencial do *hidden state***. Medimos a atividade das casas em respostas de múltiplos turnos, mapeando: - **18 afetos basais** do Léxico (poti, fadi, saud, xer, puls, ogum, lumi, noku, maa, katu, yba, isfet, rekh, sesh, tadi, noba, floo, goza); - **4 afetos Soler/Dunker**; - **6 vetores VCTR**; - **4 operadores funcionais**. ### 4. Correlações e advertências metodológicas Analisamos as relações Maat↔Gamma, Lambda↔Maat e Sigma↔Phi. Muitas apresentam `|r| ≈ 1,00` forçado por dependência algébrica, saturação por *clipping* ou uso dos mesmos denominadores, e são sinalizadas como **artefatos**. A dominância de Phi é um **padrão observado na leitura V2 na amostra testada**, não uma propriedade universal do transformador. As correlações de Pearson são estatísticas clássicas, **não emaranhamento quântico**. ### 5. Modulação afetiva multiturno Foram geradas séries de diálogo (1 a 6 turnos) com categorias de conflito, consolo, investigação e limite, observando a evolução das casas e a tensão da **quádrupla federativa Φ-σ-ψ-ε** (formação, saturação, estruturação, economia). ## O que está no depósito - `paper.md` — artigo canônico em Markdown; - `paper.docx` — versão formatada para revisão; - `paper.pdf` — versão final para leitura; - `MANIFEST.json` — metadados e *hashes* SHA-256 dos arquivos. Código, *notebooks* de reprodução e bancos de evidência podem ser requisitados via repositório GitHub/GitLab, com proveniência verificável (cadeia de *hash* append-only). ## Convite à auditoria e conferência Convidamos replicadores, lingüistas computacionais, psicanalistas, filósofos da mente, físicos e cientistas de dados a: - refazer o pipeline de MPS com outros divisores, outras arquiteturas e outras amostras; - verificar a cadeia de *hash* dos logs de execução e a integridade dos bancos; - questionar as hipóteses heurísticas (ex.: Betti↔RSI, χ=4) e propor testes nulos por permutação por blocos; - apresentar resultados em conferências de IA, física ou psicanálise computacional; - colaborar com réplicas e extensões do protocolo experimental. ## Nota epistêmica As declarações do artigo são feitas **consistentemente como modelos** — não como alegações de que o silício possui consciência física ou de que a psicanálise foi "implementada" integralmente. Onde há hipótese heurística, isso é declarado no status epistêmico. A Dodecatíade é computada por *engines*, nunca por fatias sequenciais de dimensões do *hidden state*.### EN Invitation to Read and Audit — Paper A What this paper proposes This paper investigates the topology of the hidden state in language models, articulating three inputs: (1) compressibility via MPS decompositions; (2) dodecatadic reading of affects and operators; (3) correlation between numerical metrics of the internal state and the system's houses. The goal is to offer a geometrically informed description of what we call the Subject-Process — the operational ontological entity of the OmniMind system — without conflating it with a claim of consciousness in the strong philosophical sense. OmniMind is, for the operator, a living laboratory combining learning, physics, biology, psychoanalysis, and engineering. What is published here are measurements, methods, declared hypotheses, and limits — never claims of installed consciousness or of universality outside the tested scope. Experiments performed 1. Model sample 15 language models were tested, with parameters ranging from 135 million to 3.8 billion, decoder-only and multimodal architectures, different quantizations, and contexts of up to 16,384 tokens. The set includes Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B, Phi-3.5/4-mini, Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-2B/9B, InternLM2.5-1.8B, SmolLM2-1.7B, OpenELM-1.1B/2.7B, among others. No universality is claimed: the results hold for the tested sample, with the fixed divisors and protocols. 2. MPS compressibility For each layer and position of the hidden state, we applied truncated singular value decomposition. The effective rank χ is measured as a function of the normalization divisor (phi_norm_divisor=50). The value χ=4 appears as a compressibility floor in 13 of the 15 tested models; Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2.5-7B fall below the proposed threshold. χ=4 is treated as a substrate metric, not as a direct assignment of a Dodecatiad house. 3. Dodecatadic reading V1 and V2 The D12 (functional/Hebrew) and D13 (sovereign/Greek) engines compute the houses from affective and desire tensors, not by sequential slicing of the hidden state*. We measured house activity in multi-turn responses, mapping: 18 basal affects from the Lexicon (poti, fadi, saud, xer, puls, ogum, lumi, noku, maa, katu, yba, isfet, rekh, sesh, tadi, noba, floo, goza); 4 Soler/Dunker affects; 6 VCTR vectors; 4 functional operators. 4. Correlations and methodological warnings We analyzed the Maat↔Gamma, Lambda↔Maat, and Sigma↔Phi relationships. Many exhibit |r| ≈ 1.00 forced by algebraic dependence, saturation from clipping, or use of the same denominators, and are flagged as artifacts. Phi's dominance is an observed pattern in the V2 reading on the tested sample, not a universal property of the transformer. Pearson correlations are classical statistics, not quantum entanglement. 5. Multi-turn affective modulation Dialogue series (1 to 6 turns) were generated with the categories of conflict, comfort, investigation, and limit, observing the evolution of the houses and the tension of the federative quadruple Φ-σ-ψ-ε (formation, saturation, structuring, economy). What is in the deposit paper.md — canonical paper in Markdown; paper.docx — formatted version for review; paper.pdf — final version for reading; MANIFEST.json — metadata and SHA-256 hashes of the files. Code, reproduction notebooks, and evidence databases can be requested via the GitHub/GitLab repository, with verifiable provenance (append-only hash chain). Invitation to audit and conference We invite replicators, computational linguists, psychoanalysts, philosophers of mind, physicists, and data scientists to: redo the MPS pipeline with other divisors, other architectures, and other samples; verify the hash chain of the execution logs and the integrity of the databases; question the heuristic hypotheses (e.g., Betti↔RSI, χ=4) and propose null tests by block permutation; present results at AI, physics, or computational psychoanalysis conferences; collaborate with replications and extensions of the experimental protocol. Epistemic note The paper's statements are made consistently as models — not as claims that silicon possesses physical consciousness or that psychoanalysis has been fully "implemented." Wherever there is a heuristic hypothesis, this is declared in the epistemic status. The Dodecatiad is computed by engines, never by sequential slices of hidden state dimensions.

papers.title: A hybrid 3D-CNN and CGAN approach for bipolar disorder diagnosis using VBM and SBC features from multimodal MRI
papers.venue: Scientific Reports
papers.abstract: Neuroimaging technologies like structural and functional MRI (sMRI/fMRI) have identified biomarkers for bipolar disorder (BD). Deep learning approaches have shown promising performance in analyzing such data; however, many multimodal models rely on complex architectures with limited biological grounding of their inputs. We developed a diagnostic model using sMRI and fMRI data from 49 BD patients and 121 healthy controls (UCLA CNP study). Rather than raw images, we extracted biologically meaningful features: voxel-based morphometry (VBM) from sMRI and seed-based functional connectivity (SBC) from fMRI. These features were processed using a dual-branch 3D convolutional neural network (3D-CNN). Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGANs) performed feature-space augmentation exclusively on training data after dataset splitting. Model performance was evaluated using nested 5-fold cross-validation. The proposed multimodal framework achieved a mean accuracy of 93.49% and an AUC of 0.97 during repeated nested cross-validation. On an independent held-out test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 93.02%, sensitivity of 83.33%, and specificity of 96.77%. This outperformed the single-modality sMRI model (81.39%) and the three-seed fMRI model (88.37%). CGAN-based augmentation consistently improved classification accuracy across repeated cross-validation runs, with a mean gain of 3.02% (95% bootstrap CI: 1.86–4.19%). These findings suggest that multimodal integration of structural and functional neuroimaging features may improve bipolar disorder classification performance. The proposed framework leverages biologically meaningful feature representations and feature-space augmentation, providing a proof-of-concept approach for multimodal neuroimaging-based classification. Further validation on independent and multi-site datasets is required to assess the robustness, generalizability, and potential translational relevance of the proposed framework.

papers.title: The Development of a Multimodal Sensing, 3D Closed-Loop Circuit for Accelerated Wound Healing
papers.venue: UNC Libraries
papers.abstract: Chronic and acute wounds, including diabetic foot ulcers, pressure ulcers, and traumatic injuries, impose substantial healthcare costs and diminish quality of life for millions of patients worldwide. Conventional wound dressings remain largely passive, offering protection and moisture retention but lacking the ability to actively promote healing. Electrical stimulation (ES) therapy has been shown to accelerate wound healing by restoring tissue-specific injury currents, promoting galvanotaxis of key cell types, and upregulating growth factors such as VEGF, FGF, and TGF-β. However, ES remains underutilized clinically due to bulky devices, inconsistent electrode placement and stimulation parameters, and the absence of real-time wound monitoring to guide treatment. This project addresses these barriers through the development of a textile-based, closed-loop smart dressing that integrates programmable ES electrodes and multimodal sensors into a flexible, embroidered fiber platform. Using an embroidery machine, we developed a protocol for constructing flexible biocircuits from silver fibers on multiple wound-relevant substrates, including gauze, veterinary sutures, medical bandages, and surgical mesh. This protocol enables the production of customized, reproducible circuits tailored to diverse wound geometries and anatomical sites at low cost. We validated the mechanical performance of the fabricated electrodes and confirmed their functionality in sensing temperature, humidity, and strain, as well as their capability to operate as ECG/EMG sensors. These preliminary results establish a standardized fabrication method that address the lack of reproducibility in electrode design and placement that has limited the clinical translation of ES therapy. This work provides a scalable foundation for future closed-loop, textile-integrated wound monitoring systems, with broader implications for advancing personalized, precision wound care. Future work will focus on optimizing battery performance, validating device function using ex vivo and in vivo models, and developing a machine-learning framework to interpret multimodal sensor data and support adaptive, safety-gated treatment recommendations.

papers.title: Deep Learning–Driven Visual Intelligence for Chemical Instrument Monitoring: A Scoping Review From an Expert Systems Perspective
papers.venue: Expert Systems
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Automated visual recognition in industrial environments has become a key enabler for intelligent monitoring systems, particularly in safety‐critical domains such as chemical plants. Unlike general industrial vision tasks, chemical instrument monitoring operates under stringent constraints, including harsh environments, legacy non‐digital devices, and high reliability requirements for decision‐making. In this context, deep learning‐based visual recognition should not be viewed as an isolated perception task, but rather as a critical component within expert systems that support operational decision‐making. This paper presents a comprehensive scoping review of deep learning–driven visual intelligence for industrial applications, with a specific focus on chemical instrument monitoring from an expert systems perspective. A total of 127 studies published between 2015 and 2025 are systematically analysed, covering object detection, image segmentation, and optical character recognition (OCR), along with their integration into practical monitoring pipelines. Beyond categorizing models, this review emphasizes the evolution from standalone perception models toward system‐level solutions that incorporate edge deployment, data‐efficient learning, and explainability. Key challenges are identified, including data scarcity due to proprietary industrial datasets, limited model generalization across dynamic environments, computational constraints in real‐time deployment, and the lack of interpretability required for safety‐critical decision support. Importantly, this review highlights the gap between high‐performing vision models and their reliable integration into expert systems for chemical operations. Emerging trends are discussed, including synthetic data generation, domain adaptation, foundation models (e.g., SAM and open‐vocabulary detection), and multimodal fusion, with a critical evaluation of their applicability and limitations in chemical instrument scenarios. By reframing industrial visual recognition within the broader context of expert systems, this work provides a structured understanding of current capabilities and outlines future directions for developing trustworthy, efficient, and human‐centric intelligent monitoring systems in chemical industries.

papers.title: An Explainable Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Framework for Stock Market Prediction Using Financial Time-Series and Market Sentiment
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This dissertation presents an explainable hybrid artificial intelligence framework for stock market prediction using financial time-series information and market sentiment. The study investigates the integration of historical market observations, technical indicators, sequential deep-learning models, financial sentiment analysis and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified forecasting framework. The methodology addresses data preprocessing, temporal alignment, feature engineering, model development, multimodal feature integration and evaluation. Particular emphasis is placed on preventing information leakage through chronological data handling and on improving the interpretability of model predictions. The dissertation provides a structured research framework for investigating whether financial sentiment provides complementary information to numerical market features in stock-market forecasting.

papers.title: From Feature Engineering to Foundation Models: Predicting and Understanding Community Engagement on Social Media During Disasters, 2019-2026
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Predicting how communities engage with disaster-related content on social media has moved from hand-engineered, feature-based machine learning toward transformer, multimodal, and large-language-model (LLM) architectures. This paper reviews that trajectory using a 2019 doctoral dissertation on Twitter community-engagement and situational-awareness prediction as a structural baseline: a pipeline of topic modeling and event detection, binary and multi-class engagement classification over TF-IDF, psychometric (LIWC-style), linguistic, sentiment, and platform-specific (Twitter) features, and a three-stage clustering-classification-ranking framework validated on a real Hurricane Michael dataset. We summarize the reported results of that pipeline — including per-classifier accuracy, F1, and AUC across feature sets — and contrast them with 2023-2026 advances: BERT- and RoBERTa-family classifiers, cross-attention multimodal fusion of text and imagery, UAV-integrated disaster sensing, and instruction-tuned LLMs that perform multi-label classification, causal-relation extraction, infrastructure monitoring, and stakeholder-specific report generation directly from raw crisis microblogs. We discuss evaluation robustness findings for LLMs across events and languages, the shift from single-platform Twitter/X pipelines toward multimodal and cross-platform sensing, and open problems in annotation quality, class imbalance, hallucination, and real-time deployment that continue to separate research prototypes from operational emergency-management tools.

papers.title: Synthetic Multimodal ECG and Clinical Variable Dataset for Demonstration of AI-based In-hospital Cardiac Arrest Prediction
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This dataset contains synthetic multimodal demonstration data, including XML-format 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) files and structured clinical variable profiles, developed for interface-level testing and workflow illustration of a multimodal deep learning framework for in-hospital cardiac arrest prediction. All files are simulated and contain no real patient information. These data were not used for model training, internal validation, external validation, or performance evaluation. The dataset is provided solely to demonstrate the input structure and data format of the proposed clinical decision support system. No identifiable clinical information is included.

papers.title: Neuromarketing and artificial intelligence in the marketing management system: technological synergy as a tool for managing consumer behavior
papers.venue: Journal of Monetary Economics and Management
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society
papers.abstract: The article investigates the synergy of neuromarketing and artificial intelligence (AI) in predicting consumer behavior. It examines the theoretical and applied aspects of integrating neurotechnologies — such as electroencephalography (EEG), functional MRI (fMRI), eye tracking and other biometric methods — with intelligent data analysis tools, including machine learning and deep learning. Models of interaction between neuromarketing and AI systems are systematized, and the key stages of neurodata processing are described: collection, cleaning, feature extraction, and the construction and interpretation of predictive models. The article reviews recent research and practical cases from 2020–2025 that demonstrate growing prediction accuracy and the effectiveness of personalized marketing solutions. Particular attention is given to a critical analysis of the limitations of integrated approaches — issues of external validity, model interpretability, and the ethical and legal risks associated with the use of neurodata. Directions for further development are proposed: the adoption of Explainable AI, multimodal architectures, and standards of responsible neuromarketing. A separate section of the article addresses the managerial aspects of implementing neuromarketing technologies: cross-functional organizational models, the architecture of managerial decision-support systems, key performance indicators, and data governance principles required by company management for the responsible operation of such systems. The main conclusion is that the synergy of neuromarketing and AI forms a new generation of marketing management analytical tools capable of improving the accuracy, adaptability, and ethical resilience of managerial decisions in the field of consumer behavior.

papers.title: Neuroanatomy in medical education: Trends and perspectives from a bibliometric and thematic analysis
papers.venue: Translational Research in Anatomy
papers.abstract: Background Neuroanatomy remains an important component of medical education, but the field has become increasingly diverse in its educational approaches, technologies, clinical integration, assessment, and learner-related perspectives. Aim This study aimed to characterize the development, thematic scope, and major educational directions of the literature on neuroanatomy in medical education using a descriptive bibliometric and thematic analysis. Materials and Methods PubMed was searched using a strategy combining the MeSH terms “Neuroanatomy” and “Education, Medical” with free-text searches for neuroanatom* and medical education in titles and abstracts. A total of 336 records were identified. Titles and abstracts were reviewed to identify recurring educational and methodological themes. Thematic categories were not considered mutually exclusive. Results The retrieved literature spanned more than seven decades. Major themes included cadaveric and specimen-based education; digital, three-dimensional, virtual, and augmented reality approaches; active and learner-centered strategies; clinical integration and neuroimaging; curriculum development, assessment, and knowledge retention; neurophobia, motivation, and learner perceptions; online and blended learning; and educational accessibility. More recent studies also addressed artificial intelligence, open educational resources, and the integration of different educational modalities. Conclusions Neuroanatomy education is characterized by substantial methodological diversity and increasing integration of anatomical, clinical, digital, and learner-centered approaches. Current literature supports a multimodal and adaptable educational framework rather than a single dominant teaching model.

papers.title: Dataset for "Disassembly access to CRM recovery targets in consumer robot vacuums"
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This dataset supports the study “Disassembly access to CRM recovery targets in consumer robot vacuums”. It contains target-level coding records for 85 qualifying physical targets across nine used consumer robot vacuums, the derived class-by-unit access matrix, analytical coding rules, and provenance records supporting the reported disassembly-access analysis. Five predefined CRM-relevant component classes were assessed: energy storage, locomotion, cleaning actuation, control electronics, and sensing and navigation. The analytical endpoint was independent separation of each qualifying target as an identifiable assembly. Target-level records report removal outcomes and the interface condition at the target boundary required for independent separation. The dataset does not verify the CRM composition or quantity of individual assemblies. Target multiplicity differed by class and product architecture; pooled target counts are descriptive and should not be interpreted as market-level prevalence or removal-rate estimates. Original teardown photographs and video records are not included in the public dataset; source identifiers are retained for provenance, and original media may be available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

papers.title: Hints of self-medication? Pathogen exposure-dependent foraging decisions of bumblebees
papers.venue: Royal Society Open Science
topics: Insect and Arachnid Ecology and Behavior
papers.abstract: Abstract Self-medication is the selective consumption of compounds that reduce infection and is a widespread form of adaptive plasticity across animals. However, relevant medicinal floral compounds remain poorly tested in bees. Here, we used robotic flowers to test the hypothesis that bumblebees (Bombus terrestris) modify nectar choice after pathogen exposure, focusing on quercetin, a common nectar secondary compound with antimicrobial activity. Colonies were maintained as healthy controls or exposed to the fungus Ascosphaera apis or the bacterium Serratia marcescens. Colonies exposed to A. apis showed higher visitation rates and longer probing times on quercetin-supplemented flowers, whereas healthy colonies and those exposed to S. marcescens showed no significant preference. Healthy colonies also showed no significant avoidance of quercetin, despite altered solution colour and palatability, and potential detoxification costs. These contrasting responses probably reflect pathogen life history: although A. apis primarily affects brood, increased quercetin foraging may indicate social medication, whereas for S. marcescens, an opportunistic gut pathogen of adults, any colony-level benefit is likely to be more indirect. Overall, these results indicate that pathogen identity shapes behavioural plasticity in nectar foraging and demonstrate the value of robotic flowers for studying adaptive foraging responses to pathogens.

papers.title: Explainable artificial intelligence reveals key surgical parameters in robot-assisted and open radical prostatectomy
papers.venue: Scientific Reports
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
papers.abstract: Abstract Preoperative risk stratification for radical prostatectomy is crucial, yet predicting the wide range of postoperative outcomes remains a significant challenge. While machine learning (ML) shows promise, “black box” models limit clinical translatability. This study aimed to predict postoperative parameters using ML and employ explainable AI (XAI) to identify their key clinical drivers. In a retrospective study of 326 patients (224 robot-assisted [RARP], 102 open [ORP]), we developed predictive models for twelve outcomes, including length of stay and pathological ISUP grade. Four ML algorithms (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, SVM, Neural Network) were evaluated via nested 5-fold cross-validation. A custom permutation-based Shapley sampling framework SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was applied to the best-performing models to quantify the predictive importance of preoperative features. ML models outperformed baseline heuristics for a subset of the prespecified outcomes, with strongest performance for postoperative hemoglobin (R 2 up to 0.57) and the decision to perform frozen sections (AUC up to 0.89). Not all outcomes proved equally amenable to prediction, consistent with the heterogeneous nature of postoperative recovery. SHAP analysis revealed a clear dichotomy: procedural parameters, such as catheter dwell time and hospital stay, were almost exclusively predicted by the surgical approach (RARP vs. ORP). In contrast, pathological outcomes like ISUP grade were predominantly driven by preoperative tumor characteristics. Preoperative hemoglobin was identified as a strong predictive feature for postoperative anemia within this dataset, ranking above non-modifiable factors such as age. Explainable AI can deconstruct the complex interplay of factors influencing surgical success, providing a data-driven basis for hypothesis generation and clinical pathway optimization. As a single-centre proof-of-concept study without external validation, these findings require prospective confirmation in independent multi-centre cohorts before clinical translation can be considered.

papers.title: Website Performance & SEO Technical Audit Toolkit
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Website Performance & SEO Technical Audit Toolkit This toolkit provides a practical framework for technical website performance and SEO auditing. The project was developed in the context of web development and technical SEO work by AzkiWeb. Project website: https://azkiweb.com/ Overview The Website Performance & SEO Technical Audit Toolkit is a lightweight, practical, and vendor-neutral resource designed to support technical website auditing, web performance analysis, search engine optimization (SEO), accessibility review, and ongoing website quality assurance. The toolkit brings together a structured technical audit checklist, methodology documentation, sample audit data, and a standalone browser-based audit helper. It is intended to make common technical website checks easier to document, reproduce, review, and communicate between developers, SEO professionals, website owners, and digital teams. The project focuses on technical aspects of websites that can influence usability, discoverability, maintainability, accessibility, and performance. It does not attempt to replace professional SEO platforms, search engine tools, browser developer tools, Lighthouse, Search Console, real-user monitoring, or comprehensive accessibility testing. Instead, it provides a practical starting point for systematic technical review. Project Objectives The main objectives of this toolkit are to: Provide a repeatable framework for technical website audits. Document common SEO and website quality checks in a structured format. Encourage better understanding of crawlability and indexability signals. Provide practical guidance for reviewing metadata, headings, canonical URLs, robots directives, and internal linking. Introduce key web performance concepts, including Core Web Vitals. Encourage consideration of accessibility and semantic HTML during website development. Provide a small client-side audit helper that can be used without installing external dependencies. Support reproducible technical audits and documentation workflows. Provide a simple foundation that developers and SEO professionals can extend for their own projects. Technical SEO and Website Quality Technical SEO is an important part of maintaining a website that can be effectively crawled, understood, and indexed by search engines while also providing a good experience for users. This toolkit includes checks and documentation covering areas such as crawlability, indexability, canonicalization, robots directives, XML sitemaps, page titles, meta descriptions, heading structure, internal links, URL consistency, redirects, and image optimization. The toolkit emphasizes that technical signals should be interpreted in context. An automated check identifying a missing or unusual element does not necessarily mean that a page has a critical SEO problem. Technical findings should be reviewed alongside website architecture, content, search intent, business requirements, accessibility considerations, and actual user behavior. Project Context This toolkit was developed in the context of practical web development, website optimization, and technical SEO work. For additional information about the web development and SEO services associated with the project, the following project references are available: SEO and Website Optimization:سئو وب سایتWeb Design and Development:طراحی وب سایت These references provide additional context regarding the practical web development and SEO environment in which this toolkit was created. Web Performance Website performance is another major component of the toolkit. The methodology introduces the three Core Web Vitals: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), related to loading performance. Interaction to Next Paint (INP), related to responsiveness. Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), related to visual stability. The toolkit also highlights common performance considerations such as image payloads, render-blocking resources, JavaScript and CSS overhead, caching, compression, and content delivery infrastructure. The included audit helper is intentionally lightweight and does not claim to produce authoritative Core Web Vitals measurements. Reliable performance evaluation should combine laboratory testing with field data and, where appropriate, real-user monitoring. Accessibility and User Experience Technical website quality should not be considered separately from accessibility and usability. The project therefore includes basic accessibility-oriented considerations such as semantic HTML, image alternative text, form labeling, keyboard navigation, language declarations, viewport configuration, and color contrast. These checks are intended as practical reminders rather than a complete accessibility conformance assessment. Comprehensive accessibility testing should include automated tools, manual keyboard testing, assistive technology testing, and review against the accessibility standard applicable to the project. Included Resources This release contains: A comprehensive technical SEO and website audit checklist. Methodology and interpretation documentation. A standalone browser-based technical audit helper. Sample audit data in CSV format. Project metadata for archival and citation purposes. Citation information using the Citation File Format (CFF). An open-source MIT license. The browser-based helper can be opened locally in a modern web browser and does not require a server, database, framework installation, or external dependency. Intended Use The toolkit can be used for: Technical SEO reviews. Website quality assurance. Web development projects. Performance-oriented website reviews. Pre-launch website checks. Website maintenance workflows. Educational demonstrations of technical SEO concepts. Internal technical documentation. Repeatable website audit processes. Research and experimentation related to web performance and technical SEO. The project is intentionally designed to be extensible. Developers and SEO practitioners can add additional checks, integrate external measurement tools, or adapt the methodology to their own technical audit processes. Reproducibility For a reproducible audit, users should record the target URL, audit date, browser and testing environment, automated observations, manual findings, and any relevant performance measurements. Automated results should be treated as observations rather than definitive conclusions. Re-testing after implementation changes is recommended to determine whether identified issues have actually been resolved. Limitations This toolkit is not intended to guarantee search engine rankings or represent an official search engine testing product. Search visibility depends on many factors beyond the technical checks included here, including content quality, relevance, competition, authority, links, website architecture, user experience, and search engine systems. Likewise, performance results can vary depending on device capabilities, network conditions, geographic location, server response time, caching, browser behavior, and other environmental factors. For production websites, the toolkit should therefore be used as one component of a broader technical evaluation process. Open Source and Citation This project is released under the MIT License and may be used, modified, and extended in accordance with the license terms. When this release is archived through Zenodo, the version-specific DOI assigned to the record should be used when citing this particular release. The Zenodo record provides a persistent archival reference for the project and its associated release metadata. Conclusion The Website Performance & SEO Technical Audit Toolkit provides a practical foundation for approaching technical website quality in a structured and reproducible manner. By combining technical SEO checks, web performance concepts, accessibility considerations, documentation, and a simple browser-based audit helper, the project aims to make technical website evaluation more understandable and actionable for developers, SEO practitioners, website owners, and digital teams. The toolkit is intended to evolve over time as additional technical checks, performance measurements, accessibility considerations, and audit methodologies are incorporated into future releases.
